# `response-error-status-added`

New 4xx/5xx response documented

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `wire` |
| **Default severity** | `info` |
| **Rule IDs** | `response-error-status-added` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M3) |
| **Group** | Responses ([RULES.md section 6](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A new 4xx or 5xx response was documented.

## Why this default

Clients already have to handle errors; documenting one more is usually just documentation.

## Example

From test case [`response-error-status-added`](../../test/cases/response-error-status-added/): A new 404 documented.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
                schema:
                  type: object
+         '404':
+           description: not found
```

Findings:

- `response-error-status-added` · info · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. See [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  response-error-status-added: info
```
